record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
record.original_question: Why do the Martini and IFIC/Nieves RPA-based calculations for carbon neutrino CCQE-like scattering integrated over the MiniBooNE flux give a two-particle–two-hole (2p–2h) contribution that differs by about a factor of two, and is the unresolved axial-response enhancement responsible for this difference?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider charged-current quasi-elastic-like (CCQE-like) scattering of muon neutrinos on a carbon-12 target, integrated over the MiniBooNE muon-neutrino flux. Two microscopic many-body calculations of this process, both based on a local Fermi gas description of the nucleus together with Random Phase Approximation (RPA) long-range correlations and an explicit two-particle–two-hole (2p–2h) multinucleon excitation channel — namely (i) the model of Martini and collaborators and (ii) the IFIC/Valencia model of Nieves and collaborators — produce flux-integrated total CCQE-like cross sections that are in reasonable mutual agreement, but their separate 2p–2h contributions differ by approximately a factor of two, with the Martini 2p–2h piece being the larger.

(a) Identify the physical and formal origins of this factor-of-two discrepancy in the 2p–2h contribution. In particular, account for differences in (i) the set of diagrams included (pionic, Δ-mediated, exchange, and interference terms), (ii) the treatment of in-medium pion and Δ propagators and short-range correlations (e.g., Landau–Migdal g′ parameters), (iii) the kinematic phase space and energy–momentum-transfer regions actually integrated, and (iv) the precise definition of what is labelled "n-particle n-hole" in each formalism versus n-body currents used elsewhere.

(b) Determine whether an enhancement of the isovector axial nuclear response (beyond the standard RPA quenching that is well established for the isovector spin-longitudinal channel) is present in one calculation but not the other, and decide whether such an axial-response enhancement is the dominant cause of the factor-of-two difference in the 2p–2h contribution.
artifact.status_search_result: The discrepancy between the Martini et al. and Nieves et al. RPA-based 2p–2h predictions for MiniBooNE CCQE-like scattering on carbon remains an active and unresolved topic. Subsequent generator-implementation studies (e.g., NEUT and GENIE comparisons) and recent reviews still report the factor-of-two gap and treat the underlying axial-response enhancement as an open issue under investigation; no community-accepted resolution has appeared.

status_evidence.title: Testing CCQE and 2p2h models in the NEUT neutrino interaction generator (Wilkinson et al., 1601.05592)
status_evidence.snippet: Fits suppress the Nieves 2p2h component to 27% of nominal, and the Martini model gives substantially larger 2p2h cross sections than Nieves.
status_evidence.claim: Tension between Martini and Nieves 2p2h predictions persists in generator-level fits to MiniBooNE/MINERvA data.

status_evidence.title: Implementation of the Martini-Ericson-Chanfray-Marteau RPA-based model in GENIE (2508.13939)
status_evidence.snippet: Implements the Martini RPA + 2p2h model in GENIE and contrasts it with the Nieves model still used as default.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2025 the two models are still being compared rather than reconciled, indicating the discrepancy is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: CCQE, 2p2h excitations and ν-energy reconstruction (Nieves, 1304.1032)
status_evidence.snippet: Notes that the IFIC 2p2h contribution is roughly a factor of two smaller than that of Martini et al., and discusses possible origins.
status_evidence.claim: The factor-of-two difference in 2p2h between the two RPA-based calculations is documented but not resolved.
